mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation models and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0% (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates worsening labor market conditions, which typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS <= 2.0) signals stagflation risk, which triggers a sell-off in equities, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL > 3.0 AND FEDFUNDS <= 2.0) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (marked by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand for housing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST falls below 900 (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 105.0 (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below its 12-month moving average signals an easing monetary policy stance, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (RSAFS) above 380,000 million dollars indicates robust consumer demand, which typically drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS exceeds 380,000 (using 12-month rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) and rising unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5) signals a dual economic shock, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (INDPRO < 105.0 AND UNRATE > 5.5) over any 3-year rolling window.
